choices.content: Construct the midpoint of \(AB\) and draw a perpendicular to \(l\) through the midpoint. Its foot is \(P\).
Draw a perpendicular to \(l\) through \(A\). Its foot is \(P\).
Construct the perpendicular bisector of \(AB\). Its intersection with \(l\) is \(P\).
Construct \(A'\), the reflection of \(A\) across \(l\), and draw \(A'B\). Its intersection with \(l\) is \(P\).

question.prompt: \(A\) and \(B\) lie on the same side of line \(l\). How can a point \(P\) be found on \(l\) to minimize \(PA+PB\)?

solutions.explanation: \(PA=PA'\), so \(PA+PB=PA'+PB\), which is minimized when \(A'\), \(P\), and \(B\) are collinear.
solutions.title: Reflect and straighten the path
